legacy_root.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:RES-0082 in the receipt AND an explicit answer or NOT-ESTABLISHED verdict on partitioned independence, with human and LLM evidence reported separately
legacy_root.question: What is the measured effect of anonymizing participants and partitioning their evidence, and does partitioning genuinely restore independence for identical-model participants — the mechanism the 05-ECO anti-adoption prescribes instead of adding reviewers?

answer.human_rail: In humans, partitioning evidence (hidden profiles) harms accuracy: Stasser & Titus 1985 Table 3, 18% vs 83% chose the superior candidate; Lu, Yuan & McLeod 2012, eight times less likely than full-information groups (65 studies / 3,189 groups). Independent elicitation (withholding others' estimates — Lorenz et al. 2011 Fig. 1–2, N=144) preserves diversity; social information drops the wisdom-of-crowd indicator by ~1 unit on a 0–6 scale without cutting collective error. Name-anonymity in GSS is reported to raise idea counts (Connolly et al. 1990) but that headline is E3 here because cell means were not recovered.
answer.llm_rail: In LLMs, identical-model copies are measurably non-independent even when the input is reordered rather than partitioned: Zheng et al. Table 2 GPT-4 swap-consistency 65.0% (baseline 100%); Wang et al. Table 2 ChatGPT conflict 82.5% (66/80). Li et al. 2026 InfoDelphi then shows that splitting evidence across three copies of the *same* gpt-5.4-mini improves Brier 0.178 vs 0.193 (all-public) on PolyGym N=375, with 1.7× inter-agent variance. That is a Brier effect, not an independence proof: Proposition 3.1 *assumes* private-error covariance is zero, and Figure 4 still shows 73% variance collapse after two deliberation rounds.
answer.identical_model_partition_sentence: NOT-ESTABLISHED: partitioning does not have a published measurement that identical-model participants become statistically independent (error correlation restored to ~0).

identical_model_partition.question: does partitioning restore independence for identical models
identical_model_partition.rationale: The nearest same-model test (InfoDelphi, three gpt-5.4-mini copies) reports Brier/accuracy and inter-agent forecast variance, not a measured pairwise error correlation of zero. The decorrelation formula treats Cov(ε_priv_i, ε_priv_j)=0 as an assumption. The authors note retrieved documents share topical correlation, so the independence bound is approximate. After deliberation, BM25-routed agents still lose 73% of inter-agent variance. Adjacent LLM-judge order-swap studies (Zheng Table 2, Wang Table 2) show the same weights plus reordered evidence still disagree with themselves. Therefore independence restoration is NOT-ESTABLISHED.

nearest_measured_effect.baseline: identical-model all-public debate on PolyGym N=375

mechanisms.canonical_mechanism: Partitioning evidence across human discussants (the hidden-profile design) reliably *reduces* group accuracy relative to shared full information, because discussion samples common items.
Across the hidden-profile literature, partitioned unique information is undersampled and hidden-profile groups fail far more often than full-information groups.
mechanisms.effect_size: eight times less likely to find the solution; +2 SD common vs unique mentions

mechanisms.canonical_mechanism: Withholding others' estimates (the operational form of independent, anonymous elicitation in estimation tasks) preserves crowd diversity; even mild social information collapses diversity without improving collective error.
mechanisms.effect_size: wisdom-of-crowd indicator ~1 unit lower on a 0–6 scale under information exchange
mechanisms.baseline: no-information control, N=144, five sequential estimates

mechanisms.canonical_mechanism: Two copies of the same LLM judge, given the same pair in swapped order, are not independent: consistency is far below 100% and first/second position bias is large.
mechanisms.baseline: order-independent judge would be 100% consistent under swap

mechanisms.canonical_mechanism: Designed public/private evidence split among identical-model copies improves Brier score versus all-public debate. This is a forecasting gain, not a demonstration that error correlation has been restored to zero.
mechanisms.effect_size: Brier 0.178 at ρ=0.5 vs 0.193 at ρ=1.0 (Acc 77.9% vs 75.7%); variance 1.7× vs homogeneous
mechanisms.baseline: identical gpt-5.4-mini copies with all-public evidence (ρ=1.0); Standard Debate Brier 0.202

mechanisms.canonical_mechanism: Anonymous GSS groups with a critical confederate produced the most original solutions (Connolly, Jessup & Valacich 1990).
mechanisms.effect_size: greatest number of original solutions (no cell mean recovered)
mechanisms.note: E3: headline without baseline cannot promote a mechanism

supports: same-model evidence split can improve Brier
contradicts: partitioning evidence among discussing humans does not by itself yield a better group decision

anti_adoption_2.paraphrase: Do not add a second same-vendor reviewer on the same input; partition the evidence instead.
anti_adoption_2.implication_from_this_unit: For humans, partitioning is not a free independence restore — hidden profiles go the other way unless aggregation stays independent (Lorenz). For identical LLMs, partitioning can help Brier (InfoDelphi) but independence restoration is NOT-ESTABLISHED.
